question: A city reservoir tracked its total million-gallon level throughout the week, starting with 133 million gallons on Monday. On Tuesday, 109 million gallons were released downstream. On Wednesday, a rainstorm added 60 million gallons. On Thursday, another storm added 40 million gallons. On Friday, a third storm added 24 million gallons. On Saturday, evaporation removed 63 million gallons from the tracked level. A separate reservoir across the valley, unrelated to this one, held 900 million gallons. On Sunday, converting the tracked level into a percentage-of-capacity figure — a simple unit change — the utility multiplied the tracked number by 8. How many did the tracked percentage figure come to by Sunday?

A toy company tracked the total number of action figures produced on Line 1, starting with 209 figures. A record shift multiplied the tracked count by 9. A second shift doubled it again. The figures were then split evenly into two shipping batches, and only the first batch's count was tracked. A dozen quality inspectors checked the line that day, though that number has nothing to do with the tracked count. A late addition added 47 more figures to the tracked batch. A bulk order then multiplied the tracked batch by 8. A separate production line, unrelated to this batch, made 600 figures. Finally, a bonus run added 48 more to the tracked batch. How many figures were in the tracked batch?

A dairy farm tracked the total gallons of milk in the morning collection tank, starting with 55 gallons at dawn. By mid-morning, a second herd's milking tripled the tracked volume. By midday, a third herd's milking multiplied the tracked volume by 9. By afternoon, a late collection added 65 more gallons. Converting the tracked volume from gallons to liters for the co-op's export report — a simple unit change — the farm multiplied the tracked number by 7 that evening. How many liters did the tracked total come to by evening?

A chicken coop had 12 eggs collected at dawn. By mid-morning, half of them had been set aside for hatching, and only the hatching batch was tracked from then on. By midday, each of those eggs was found to represent a clutch of 7 once counted per hen, multiplying the tracked count. By afternoon, a second coop's clutches were merged in, multiplying the tracked count by 9. By evening, a third merger multiplied the tracked count by 6. A separate coop across the yard, unrelated to this one, had 40 eggs. By night, a final gathering added 80 more to the tracked count. How many eggs did the tracked count show by night?

Manager Osei tracked the total dollars in Store A's daily deposit, starting with 114 dollars from early sales. Her regional counterpart, manager Vance, tracked Store B's deposit separately, which totaled 900 dollars, but only Store A is tracked here. A midmorning rush multiplied Store A's tracked deposit by 7. A lunch rush multiplied it by 5 more. An afternoon sale added 14 more dollars. An evening sale added 56 more dollars. Finally, a bank deposit fee removed 2162 dollars from the tracked total. How many dollars were left in Store A's tracked deposit?

A construction crew tracked the total cubic yards of concrete remaining in the mixer truck, starting with 224 cubic yards at the start of the pour. During the morning, 74 cubic yards were poured for the foundation. By midday, 64 more cubic yards were poured for a retaining wall. In the afternoon, 1 more cubic yard was used for patching. By late afternoon, a second truck's load quadrupled the tracked remaining volume. By evening, a large driveway pour used 291 cubic yards from the tracked total. A dozen workers were on site that day, though that number has nothing to do with the tracked volume. Finally, at night, a matching third truck multiplied the tracked total by 6. How many cubic yards of concrete were tracked by night?

A brewery tracked the total gallons of beer in Fermenter 2 throughout the day, starting with 116 gallons at dawn. By mid-morning, the batch was split evenly into 4 smaller fermenters, and only the first one's volume was tracked from then on. By midday, a fresh addition multiplied the tracked fermenter's volume by 5. By afternoon, a doubling technique doubled the tracked volume again. Converting the tracked volume into a case-count estimate for distribution — a simple unit change — the brewery added 63 more to the tracked total that evening. How many cases did the tracked total come to by evening?

Trader Aoki tracked the total number of bonds in his fixed-income portfolio, starting with 157 bonds. His colleague, trader Beckham, held a portfolio with a mere dozen bonds by comparison, but only Aoki's portfolio is tracked here. A bulk purchase multiplied his tracked bond count by 6. A market shift then meant selling off 202 bonds. A further downturn cost him 521 more bonds. A final adjustment removed 61 more bonds. Finally, a leveraged buy multiplied his tracked total by 7. How many bonds were in Aoki's tracked portfolio after the leveraged buy?

A charity tracked the total dollars in its silent auction fund throughout gala night, starting with 158 dollars raised before doors opened. During the cocktail hour, 38 more dollars came in. During dinner, 24 more dollars came in. During the live auction, a matching donor multiplied the tracked fund by 7. During dessert, a second matching donor doubled the tracked fund again. A separate raffle at the same gala, unrelated to this fund, brought in 500 dollars. By the end of the night, a large venue bill took 1136 dollars out of the tracked fund. How many dollars were in the silent auction fund by the end of the night?

Delivery driver Han tracked the total packages left in his van throughout his route, starting with 178 packages at the depot. His coworker, driver Osei, ran a separate route with 90 packages, but only Han's van is tracked here. By midmorning, 95 packages had been delivered and removed from the tracked count. By midday, a depot run added 29 more packages. By afternoon, a route merge doubled the tracked count. By evening, a second merge multiplied the tracked count by 6. How many packages were in Han's van by evening?

A construction site tracked the total feet of electrical wire on the main spool, starting with 225 feet. A first-floor wiring job used 189 feet. The remaining wire's tracked length was then tripled once a matching spool was added in. A second delivery added 38 more feet. A third delivery added 29 more feet. Converting the tracked length from feet to meters for the European supplier's invoice — a simple unit change — the crew subtracted 1 unit for a rounding correction. How many meters did the tracked total come to?

Rancher Whitcombe tracked the total number of sheep in the east pasture, starting with 196 sheep. His neighbor, rancher Doyle, kept a separate flock of 900 sheep, but only Whitcombe's east pasture is tracked here. A lambing season multiplied his tracked flock by 8. A sale to a nearby market then removed 978 sheep. A merger with another flock doubled the tracked count. A late addition added 29 more sheep. The flock was then split evenly among 3 grazing fields, and only the first field's count was tracked. Finally, a purchase added 74 more sheep to the tracked field. How many sheep were in the tracked field?

Chef Otto tracked the total pounds of flour in his bakery's main bin, starting with 158 pounds. His fellow chef, Ingrid, tracked a separate bin of sugar holding 900 pounds, but only Otto's flour bin is tracked here. A bulk delivery tripled the tracked flour. A second delivery multiplied it by 6 more. A small top-off added 57 more pounds. A big weekend of baking used up 182 pounds from the tracked bin. Converting the remaining flour into a loaf-count estimate — a simple unit change — Otto multiplied the tracked number by 4. How many loaves did the tracked estimate come to?

A tech blog tracked its total daily page views throughout launch day, starting with 213 views at sunrise. By morning, a front-page feature quadrupled the tracked view count. By midday, a viral share multiplied it by 7. By afternoon, a second share multiplied it by 5. By evening, a trending badge multiplied it by 6. By night, a server outage caused half the tracked views to be lost from the log. How many views did the tracked log show by night?

A farmers market tracked the total pounds of apples at the orchard stand throughout the day, starting with 136 pounds at opening. During the morning, a delivery added 52 more pounds. By midday, another delivery added 53 more pounds. A dozen market vendors set up nearby, though that number has nothing to do with the tracked apple weight. In the afternoon, a bulk order doubled the tracked apple weight after a matching donation came in. A separate stand selling pears, unrelated to this one, had 90 pounds. By evening, a final delivery added 71 more pounds. How many pounds of apples did the tracked stand have by evening?

Skater Nadia tracked the total points in her figure skating routine's running score, starting with 85 points from her first element. Her rival, skater Yui, had a separate routine worth a mere dozen points at that stage, but only Nadia's score is tracked here. A deduction for a wobbled landing cost her 83 points. A spin element added 46 more points. A footwork sequence added 4 more points. A jump combination added 54 more points. Finally, the judges' bonus multiplier multiplied her tracked score by 8. How many points did Nadia's tracked score show after the bonus?

Analyst Voss tracked the total number of units in his company's inventory system, starting with 194 units. His colleague, analyst Preet, tracked a separate warehouse's inventory of a mere dozen units, but only Voss's system is tracked here. A large restock multiplied his tracked count by 8. A second restock multiplied it by 8 again. A massive recall then removed 11693 units from the tracked total. Converting the remaining units from individual items to full pallets for the shipping manifest — a simple unit change — Voss multiplied the tracked count by 8 once more. How many pallets did the tracked total represent?

Landscaper Priya tracked the total square feet of sod laid in the Thompson yard, starting with 113 square feet. Her assistant, Dario, was laying sod in a separate yard measuring 900 square feet, but only the Thompson yard is tracked here. A morning delivery added 28 more square feet. An afternoon delivery added 5 more. Converting the tracked area into a roll-count estimate — a simple unit change — the crew multiplied the tracked number by 7. A large order from a rival job then used up 981 of the tracked rolls. Finally, a doubled order multiplied the tracked roll count by 2. How many rolls did the tracked count come to?

A pharmacy tracked the total number of pills in a large stock bottle, starting with 143 pills. A prescription used 72 pills. A second prescription used 41 more. A third prescription used 22 more. The pharmacist then repackaged the remainder into 7-pill travel packs, multiplying the tracked count by 7 to represent the total pills across all packs — converting from bottle count to pack-pill count, a simple unit change. Finally, a damaged pack removed 6 pills from the tracked total. How many pills did the tracked pack total show?

A choir director tracked the total number of sheet music folders needed for the concert, starting with 36 folders for the main choir. A guest choir joining meant tripling the tracked folder count. The folders were then split evenly into 3 identical filing boxes, and only the first box's count was tracked. A dozen new music stands were also ordered, though that number has nothing to do with the folder count. A regional festival then multiplied the tracked box's folder count by 8. Finally, a citywide event multiplied that count by 7. How many folders did the tracked box need for the citywide event?

A charity tracked the total dollars in its bake sale cash box, starting with 25 dollars in starting change. A morning sale added 29 more dollars. A refund for a burnt batch removed 43 dollars. An afternoon sale added 18 more dollars. A dozen volunteers ran the booth that day, though that number has nothing to do with the cash total. Converting the tracked total into a token-count for the raffle — a simple unit change — the total was tripled. A matching sponsor then tripled the tracked token count once more. How many tokens did the tracked total come to?

Baker Wen tracked the total dollars in her cupcake stand's earnings box, starting with 74 dollars. Her cousin, baker Lila, ran a separate stand with 500 dollars in earnings, but only Wen's box is tracked here. A morning rush added 46 dollars. A big refund for a wrong order removed 73 dollars. Converting her tracked earnings from dollars to a loyalty-point system — a simple unit change — Wen multiplied the tracked total by 4. A bonus weekend event then multiplied the tracked points by 3. How many points did Wen's tracked total show by the end of the weekend?

A city tracked the total number of streetlights installed downtown throughout the renovation, starting with 187 streetlights already up. A dozen crews worked the project, though that number has nothing to do with the tracked light count. A first phase added 42 more streetlights. A second phase added 69 more. A citywide expansion multiplied the tracked count by 7. A grant-funded extension doubled the tracked count once more. A separate suburb, unrelated to this project, installed 500 streetlights. Finally, an audit found 1943 streetlights had been double-counted and removed them from the tracked total. How many streetlights did the tracked downtown count show after the audit?

A city tracked the total number of bicycles available at the downtown bike-share station, starting with 209 bicycles at dawn. A morning delivery added 4 more bicycles. During the morning commute, 69 bicycles were checked out and not returned. A midday delivery added 7 more bicycles. Finally, an expansion event multiplied the station's tracked bicycle count by 5. How many bicycles did the tracked station show after the expansion?

A gas station tracked the total gallons of fuel in its emergency reserve tank, starting with 59 gallons at dawn. During the morning, a delivery added 10 more gallons. By midday, a generator test used 43 gallons from the tank. In the afternoon, a small leak lost 1 more gallon. By evening, a large delivery added 79 more gallons. Converting the tracked volume from gallons to liters for the corporate report — a simple unit change — the station multiplied the tracked number by 6 that night. How many liters did the tracked reserve show by night?
